entries.summary: House bill to set a national AI framework, require a federal AI plan and establish a temporary moratorium preempting certain state laws that restrict AI models and systems in interstate commerce. entries.summary: DOE announcement that CMEI is divided into three pillars, effective immediately. It says IACC oversees state and community energy and weatherization programs and does not mention Indian Energy or Tribal rebates.

entries.title: IE Strategic Plan (Office of Indian Energy)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Four Tribal-focused goals (access and costs, workforce, energy wealth, permitting) with 2030 targets of $2 billion in cost savings, 100 MW of generation and 450 Tribal-led projects. It names no technology targets.

entries.title: Indian Energy Programs at the Department of Energy (CRS IF11793)
entries.summary: CRS overview of DOE Indian energy programs. It covers IE and the Loan Programs Office, the Tribal Energy Loan Guarantee Program's funding after the 2025 rescission, and the FY2026 request's proposed exclusion of solar, wind and battery work.

entries.title: Indian Energy Programs at the Department of Energy (CRS IF11793), February 2026 changes

entries.summary: Explains GAO's findings on DOE's Tribal energy loan guarantee program, including 20 applications and one closed guarantee, and DOE's response that the program remains open for business.

entries.title: Entities Wholly Owned by Indian Tribal Governments (TD 10039), final rule
entries.summary: Final rule treating Section 17 and Section 3 corporations and wholly owned Tribal entities as instrumentalities that make their own elective-pay elections, for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

entries.title: Elective pay and transferability frequently asked questions: Elective pay
entries.summary: IRS FAQ confirming that Indian Tribal governments are eligible for elective pay, that pre-filing registration is required and renewed each tax year, and listing 12 covered credits, including 45Y, 48E and 45W.

entries.title: Highlights of the new sections 45Y and 48E wind and solar beginning-of-construction guidance
entries.summary: Summarizes the 2025 reconciliation law's wind and solar deadlines and Notice 2025-42, which removed the 5% safe harbor except for small solar. It predates the June 2026 court ruling.

entries.title: Court Vacates IRS Notice 2025-42: 5% Safe Harbor for Wind and Solar Facilities Reinstated
entries.summary: Reports the June 6, 2026 D.D.C. decision in Oregon Environmental Council v. IRS (No. CV-25-4400), which set aside Notice 2025-42 in full. The 5% safe harbor is restored until new guidance or an appeal changes it.

entries.title: Archived Interior release on the first Tribal Electrification Program awards
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior (Indian Affairs)
entries.summary: Reports $72,181,811 in first-round awards to 21 Tribes and Tribal organizations. An archive banner says the page was published before January 20, 2025 and has not been updated.

entries.title: Tribal rebates fact sheet (Section 50122 HEEHR for Indian Tribes)
entries.summary: DOE fact sheet on the Tribal home-rebate program: about $225 million, roughly $218.25 million in formula grants and 3% held back for administration. The PDF did not parse here; the figures come from a search excerpt.

entries.title: Commerce awards $16.8 million for Tribal clean energy and resilience projects
entries.summary: Announces $16.81 million across four programs, including $11.48 million in Tribal Clean Energy Grants for solar, battery and microgrid projects and $4.75 million for Tribal electric boats.

entries.title: Power outages are getting worse on Colville Tribe homelands. New microgrids could be a big part of the solution
entries.summary: Describes three planned Colville Tribes microgrid sites (Nespelem, Paschal Sherman Indian School, Inchelium), using rooftop and canopy solar with battery backup and funded by Washington's Tribal Clean Energy grants.

entries.title: Tribal Utility Feasibility Study
entries.publisher: Schatz Energy Research Center for the Yurok Tribe (sponsor: U.S. DOE EERE)
entries.summary: Yurok Tribe study that screens energy options after a consultant ruled out a full Tribal utility, sorting them into five categories from efficiency to net-metered systems. Useful as a feasibility-method reference.

entries.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
entries.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.summary: Field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students: an unguarded GPT-4 tutor raised practice scores 48% but left students 17% below students who never had access, while a guardrailed tutor largely prevented that harm.

entries.title: From Chalkboards to Chatbots: Evaluating the Impact of Generative AI on Learning Outcomes in Nigeria
entries.publisher: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125
entries.summary: Six-week randomized trial in Nigeria of a GPT-4-based Copilot tutor: a 0.31 SD gain on a composite test and 0.23 SD on English, conditional on being designed and used properly. Sample sizes and confidence intervals were not in the text read.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
entries.publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
entries.summary: NIST's companion profile to the AI Risk Management Framework for generative AI, covering 12 risk areas such as confabulation, data privacy and human-AI configuration. The final was published in July 2024; the risk list was checked against the April 2024 draft.

entries.title: Executive Order 25-05: Data Center Workgroup
entries.publisher: Office of the Governor of Washington
entries.summary: Directs the Department of Revenue to lead a Data Center Workgroup with findings due December 1, 2025. The membership list does not name Tribal governments.

entries.title: Montana Artificial Intelligence in K-12 Education Guidelines, Version 2.0
entries.publisher: Montana Office of Public Instruction with Montana Digital Academy
entries.summary: Advisory state guidance reviewed twice a year. Lists benefits and risks, including bias, inaccuracy, overreliance and substitution for human instruction. Says better immediate task performance does not by itself show mastery, retention or transfer.

entries.title: Human-Centered AI Guidance for K-12 Public Schools (initial edition)
entries.publisher: Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction
entries.summary: First Washington K-12 AI guidance, later revised to version 3. Covers human-centered principles and student data protection. The current landing page names no Tribal sovereignty or Native-student provisions in the portion read.

entries.title: Idaho Code Title 33, Chapter 70: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Education (SB 1227)
entries.summary: Directs the State Department of Education to develop a statewide generative AI framework subject to State Board approval, and requires district and charter AI policies. Framework approved August 12, 2026 and awaiting legislative review.

entries.title: Guidance on the Use of Federal Grant Funds to Improve Education Outcomes Through Artificial Intelligence (Dear Colleague Letter)
entries.summary: Federal guidance that formula and discretionary grant funds may support AI when allowable. Encourages AI that supports educators without replacing their role, and lists responsible-use principles including privacy and stakeholder engagement.

entries.title: Navajo Nation moves to claim its data as 'inalienable' property as AI anxiety grows
entries.summary: Reports Navajo Nation Resolution NABIAU-41-26, which adopts an AI Policy Statement, declares AI data about Diné people (including language and ceremonies) inalienable, and creates a seven-member working group with a one-year study mandate.

entries.title: NTU Crafts AI Policy
entries.publisher: Tribal College Journal of American Indian Higher Education
entries.summary: Describes Navajo Technical University's approach, which leaves AI use to individual instructors (allow, restrict or ban per course) and frames the policy around student learning, academic integrity and cultural values.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Indigenous Language Revitalization: Emerging Concerns
entries.publisher: First Peoples' Cultural Council and Endangered Languages Project
entries.summary: Practitioner paper on harms in AI language tools: fabricated outputs, AI-generated vocabulary books, scraped speech data, exaggerated benefits and environmental costs. Recommends community-owned data and models, anti-scraping terms and continuing free, prior and informed consent, and includes ten questions for technology companies.

entries.title: The Performance of Artificial Intelligence in the Use of Indigenous American Languages
entries.summary: Evaluates five language models on seven Latin American Indigenous languages. Finds a significant performance gap compared with Spanish or Catalan, with limits in comprehension, expression and cultural adaptation, and scarce digital data.

entries.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
entries.summary: Defines Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility and Ethics for Indigenous data. Holds that Indigenous Peoples must determine data governance protocols, a baseline for school and language-tool data agreements.

entries.title: News Integrity in AI Assistants: An international PSM study
entries.summary: Audit of news answers from four AI assistants across 22 public service media organizations in 18 countries. 45 percent of responses had at least one significant issue; sourcing problems were the largest category (31 percent).

entries.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
entries.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (Bastani et al.)
entries.summary: Field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students. Unrestricted GPT-4 access improved practice performance but reduced later unassisted performance; a tutor giving teacher-designed hints largely mitigated the harm.

entries.title: Governor Hochul signs legislation to protect kids from AI chatbots (S.9051B/A.10379C)
entries.publisher: Office of the Governor of New York
entries.summary: Bars a dozen categories of unsafe AI companion features for users under 18, and for users whose age has not been confirmed as adult. Restrictions take effect in the coming months. Scope questions are for counsel.

entries.title: FTC Launches Inquiry into AI Chatbots Acting as Companions
entries.summary: Section 6(b) study orders to seven firms offering consumer AI chatbots (Alphabet, Character Technologies, Instagram, Meta, OpenAI, Snap, X.AI) on how they measure and limit negative effects on children and teens. A study, not an enforcement action.

entries.title: Alaska education department publishes guidelines on developing AI policies in schools
entries.summary: Reports Alaska DEED guidelines to help districts develop responsible generative AI policies. Notes that district rules range from school-level mentions of AI to a district-wide policy.

entries.title: AFN Resolution 35/2026: Protecting First Nations Environment, Sovereignty, Knowledge Systems, and Data in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Annual General Assembly resolution (carried, 1 opposed, 5 abstentions) asking AFN to oppose AI data centers on Treaty lands without consent, require OCAP-based rules for AI developers, and fund First Nations-led sovereign compute. Notes a national First Nations AI strategy expected December 2026.

entries.title: Indigenous advocates push for rights protections around AI data centers
entries.summary: Reports July 2026 EMRIP calls for FPIC on data centers, plus cases in Brazil, Chile, Alberta, Norway, Tulsa and Aotearoa. Secondary source; verify named claims.

entries.title: UN Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance: Co-Chairs' Summary
entries.summary: Summary of the inaugural Geneva Dialogue (6-7 July 2026) and its consultations. Records underrepresentation of Indigenous communities and calls for multilingual datasets including Indigenous languages.

entries.title: Call for Inputs: Study on Indigenous Peoples' right to data, including data collection and disaggregation
entries.publisher: OHCHR, Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples
entries.summary: EMRIP framing document for its 2025 data study: data collection subject to FPIC, and Indigenous data sovereignty as rights to own, control, access and possess data.

entries.title: Ensuring Indigenous Peoples' rights in the age of AI
entries.summary: Summarizes UNPFII 24th session (2025) recommendation for meaningful inclusion of Indigenous Peoples in AI development, governance and application, and risks of bias and misappropriation.

entries.title: Indigenous sovereignty in the AI era
entries.summary: Story on an EMRIP 18th session side event on AI featuring speakers from the Chickasaw Nation and the Chinook community, on stewarding Indigenous data.

entries.title: Data Sovereignty and the Kaitiakitanga License
entries.summary: Te Hiku Media explains its guardianship-based license and links a practical guide to writing a stewardship license; a working model for conditional access to Indigenous data.

entries.title: Indigenous Data Sovereignty and the Governance of Artificial Intelligence: Toward Equitable Benefit for Indigenous Peoples
entries.publisher: SAGE Publications (Prehn, Carlson, Walter, Lovett, Maher)
entries.summary: Peer-reviewed argument that AI benefits Indigenous peoples equitably only under Indigenous data sovereignty and governance, anchored in the Maiam nayri Wingara principles.

entries.title: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
entries.summary: Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, Ethics; people-and-purpose principles designed to sit alongside FAIR. Candidate crosswalk partner for TSDF tiers.

entries.title: Despite plenty of renewable energy, data centers split Norwegian society
entries.summary: Norway's data center buildout (about 90 sites, 2.79 TWh in 2025, 3.4 GW reserved) and the Sámi Parliament's suit over consultation on a gas electrification project near Hammerfest.

entries.title: Indigenous group in Brazil sues TikTok over planned data center
entries.summary: The Anacé people's federal complaint seeking suspension of permits for a TikTok data center in Ceara, citing lack of prior consultation and water concerns.

entries.title: Mihta Askiy Data Center Project (Impact Assessment Agency of Canada)
entries.summary: Federal record for the 650 MW gas-fired power facility supporting the Woodland Cree First Nation majority-owned data center; early decision that no further impact assessment is required.

entries.title: Global Indigenous Data Sovereignty Conference Communique (Canberra, 2025)
entries.publisher: Maiam nayri Wingara Indigenous Data Sovereignty Collective
entries.summary: Resources page for the Collective's principles and the 2025 global conference communique; basis for Australian Indigenous data governance work.

entries.title: AI Act (regulatory framework and implementation timeline)
entries.summary: Official EU page on Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, with the post-Omnibus timeline: high-risk Annex III rules from 2 December 2027 and Annex I from 2 August 2028.

entries.title: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
entries.summary: Voluntary tool for GPAI providers on transparency, copyright, and safety and security; useful as a public vendor due-diligence signal.

entries.title: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content
entries.summary: Voluntary code supporting AI Act Article 50 marking and labelling duties; reports about 190 signatories by end of July 2026.

entries.title: European Union ratifies the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Announces EU ratification of the first binding international AI treaty (human rights, democracy, rule of law); entry into force needs five ratifications.

entries.title: Britain steps up national defences against growing AI risks
entries.publisher: UK Government (Cabinet Office, AISI, NCSC, DCMS)
entries.summary: UK announcement on frontier AI cyber defence, serious AI incident preparedness and possible changes to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill; no frontier AI bill committed.

entries.title: Minister Solomon highlights Canada's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
entries.summary: Canada's AI for All strategy launched 4 June 2026, emphasizing safety, sovereign compute and modernized privacy and online safety law after the lapse of AIDA.

entries.title: South Korea AI Basic Act (market intelligence)
entries.summary: US government summary of the Act in force since 22 January 2026, including foreign-provider representative rules and the fines grace period.

entries.title: Japan's first AI legislation becomes law: focus on promotion, no monetary penalties
entries.summary: Law-firm analysis of Japan's May 2025 AI Promotion Act as a soft, innovation-first framework.

entries.title: India AI Impact Summit concludes with adoption of New Delhi Declaration
entries.publisher: Government of India, Press Information Bureau
entries.summary: Official release and annexed text of the voluntary New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact, with seven pillars including energy efficiency of AI systems.

entries.title: US and UK refuse to sign Paris summit declaration on inclusive AI
entries.summary: Reporting on the February 2025 Paris AI Action Summit statement signed by about 60 states, without the US and UK.

entries.title: Export control compliance for running advanced AI chips
entries.summary: Secondary analysis of the rescinded AI Diffusion Rule, the January 2026 BIS rule on H200-class exports to China, and open compliance questions; verify against BIS and the Federal Register.

entries.title: Counting (on) Indigenous Peoples: Data Sovereignty in the Age of AI
entries.summary: UN Chronicle piece arguing AI policy should be grounded in UNDRIP free, prior and informed consent across the AI life cycle.

entries.title: Tech Sovereignty: A Tribal Leader's Guide to the AI Era (webinar)
entries.summary: NCAI briefing for Tribal decision-makers on governing AI, protecting resources and data sovereignty, whether a Tribe chooses to regulate, leverage or reject AI.

entries.title: Energy Department announces over $125 million for 63 projects across 16 states
entries.summary: 63 Tribe-led projects selected for award negotiations, including 61 Tribal entities across 16 states, Alaska included. Selection is not a commitment to issue an award or provide funding. Twenty-three projects fund planning, assessment and feasibility work.

entries.title: Selected applications for DE-FOA-0003548, Unleashing Tribal Energy Development
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Selected applications by topic area with Federal Funds Requested. Includes Metlakatla, Crow Tribe, Chippewa Cree, Blackfeet Community College, Fallon Paiute-Shoshone, Bear River Band, Cape Fox Corporation and a Citizen Potawatomi Nation data center feasibility study. No Idaho entries. Details are subject to change.

entries.title: Notice of availability of the Final Supplemental EIS for the Hells Canyon Hydroelectric Project
entries.summary: FERC notice that the Final SEIS for Idaho Power's Hells Canyon project (P-1971-079) is available; the notice is dated September 4, 2026. FERC staff recommend relicensing with conditions.

entries.title: South-central Montana coal swap clears Senate committee
entries.summary: Senate Indian Affairs Committee voted 6-5 to advance S.239, the Crow Revenue Act, a land swap with the Hope family tied to a revenue-sharing deal with the Crow Tribe. Covers the 4,530 and 4,660 subsurface acre swap and a proposed revenue floor amendment.

entries.title: Montana Tribes realize long-held vision of acquiring Kerr Dam: interview with Energy Keepers CEO
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Energy Keepers, Inc. (formed fall 2012) took ownership of Kerr Dam for CSKT on Sept. 5, 2015, the first major hydro facility owned by a Tribe in the United States. FERC approved the name Seliš Ksanka Qlispe Dam on Nov. 9, 2015.

entries.title: Native American Bank provides $5.2 million financing for Metlakatla Indian Community
entries.summary: Bridge loan for Metlakatla Power & Light's intertie to Ketchikan Public Utilities, with an expected savings of nearly $150,000 a year and a return path for wind energy to the grid.

entries.title: Organized Village of Kasaan 2011 project
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: DOE planning award totaling $87,756 ($77,258 DOE, $10,498 Tribe) toward a Tribal Energy Action Plan. Performance period September 2011 to December 2012. The Tribe describes energy sources owned by distant companies.

entries.title: DOE pulls funding for Tribal energy resilience project; local partners seek path forward
entries.summary: Reports DOE's October 2, 2025 termination of 321 awards covering 223 projects, including the TERAS project led by Blue Lake Rancheria, Hoopa Valley and Yurok Tribes with RCEA, the Schatz Center and PG&E.

entries.title: Notice of preliminary permit application, Pyramid Lake Pumped Storage Project (Premium Energy Holdings)
entries.summary: Application filed November 4, 2022, to study a pumped storage project adjacent to Pyramid Lake. One alternative pairs storage with two solar farms of 1,428 MW and 572 MW.

entries.title: Coeur d'Alene Tribe saves with solar-powered rec center
entries.summary: Coeur Center rooftop solar saves about four times the original estimate. The Tribe's environmental programs manager says four utilities serve the reservation with little to no Tribal representation on any of them.

entries.title: Remote Control: rural Alaska communities seek nuanced solutions to energy system challenges
entries.summary: Rural Alaska microgrid economics. Igiugig river-current generation dates to 2019, its battery system was installed in 2022 with commissioning delayed to 2024, and electric boilers are described as dispatchable thermal loads.

entries.title: Resolution #2024-23: Establishing an ATNI Task Force on Offshore Wind Projects
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2024 Midyear Convention, Seven Feathers Casino, Canyonville, OR, May 19 to 23, 2024 (date field is the convention start). Calls for a limited-duration ATNI task force on offshore wind. A WHEREAS clause says all ATNI member Tribes are opposing continued offshore wind development at this time. The final RESOLVED clause lists outcomes from a full-stop halt to more meaningful consultation.

entries.title: ATNI Midyear Convention 2026 final draft at-a-glance agenda
entries.summary: Agenda as of 05.12.2026 for the May 17 to 21, 2026 Midyear Convention at Silver Reef Casino Resort, Ferndale, WA. Lists an Artificial Intelligence and Data Centers session (May 19) and Data Center Breakouts (May 20). Shows no resolution numbers.

entries.title: Tribal leaders talk AI, proposed legislation and national priorities at annual ATNI convention
entries.summary: Coverage of the September 2026 ATNI Annual Convention in Snoqualmie, WA. Reports an AI and data centers panel (September 15) and two AI resolutions brought forward: an ATNI task force on AI, and youth AI chatbots in schools. Extracted text includes the sentence Both passed. No resolution numbers are given.

entries.title: Tribal Nation Transmission Program (DOE Office of Indian Energy bulletin)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Federal bulletin announcing technical assistance for strategic transmission planning, open to federally recognized Tribes and Alaska Native Villages, under a new Tribal Nation Transmission Program.

entries.title: Tribal Energy Vision (2022 Energy Vision)
entries.summary: 2022 Energy Vision with 43 recommendations for the Columbia Basin and Northwest. Recommendation 31 calls for a siting plan for renewable resources and transmission lines with state, federal and regional partners.

entries.title: Data Center Workgroup: Preliminary Report
entries.summary: Preliminary report delivered to the Governor on December 1, 2025, under Executive Order 25-05. The Department of Revenue workgroup page (dor.wa.gov/about/data-center-workgroup) says the final report waits for tribal consultation to finish.

entries.title: Support of US Indigenous Data Sovereignty and Inclusion of Tribes in the Development of Tribal Data Governance Principles
entries.summary: NCAI resolution supporting Indigenous data sovereignty and Tribal inclusion in data governance principles. Cited as KAN-18-011 (June 2018) in Data Science Journal, https://datascience.codata.org/articles/10.5334/dsj-2019-031.

entries.title: Resolution #2025-49 (roadless rule), ATNI Annual Convention 2025
entries.summary: Certified as adopted at the 2025 Annual Convention, Suquamish Clearwater Casino Resort, October 12 to 16, 2025. Shows 2025 numbering reached at least 49. States that the resolution is ATNI policy until withdrawn or modified by subsequent resolutions.

entries.title: Resolution #2026-052 (West Coast oil pipeline), ATNI Annual Convention 2026
entries.summary: Certified as adopted at the 2026 Annual Convention, Snoqualmie, WA, September 13-17, 2026. Shows Annual 2026 numbering reached at least 52. Used here as an example of ATNI PDF naming and certification.

entries.title: DOE Announces Contract Selections for Intertribal Organizations To Improve Communication and Engagement for Tribal Energy Funding and Resources
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Names five regional InterTribal organizations, including ATNI, selected for a $3.6 million pilot to improve DOE funding navigation and engagement with Tribes. Awards were pending contract negotiations.

entries.title: Details About the Key Elements Agreed Between the United States and Canada Regarding Modernization of the Columbia River Treaty Regime
entries.summary: Describes the 2024 agreement in principle, including an Indigenous-led advisory body on ecosystem needs, Canadian salmon flow commitments, and coordination of Tribal and Indigenous salmon reintroduction studies.

entries.title: Final Bill Report, SSB 6355 (C 249 L 26), as enacted
entries.summary: Creates the Washington Electric Transmission Authority. Directs the Governor's Office of Indian Affairs to convene federally recognized Tribes on a statewide Tribal consultation framework for transmission planning.

entries.title: Tribal leaders talk AI, proposed legislation, and national priorities at annual Northwest convention
entries.summary: Reports an ATNI convention panel on AI and data centers. CRITFC staff warned that data center cooling water could warm Columbia Basin rivers in ways harmful to salmon.

entries.title: Controversial License to Destroy Sacred Tribal Resources Challenged in Federal Court
entries.summary: Advocacy release on Ninth Circuit petitions by Columbia Riverkeeper and the Yakama Nation challenging FERC's January 2026 license for the Goldendale pumped-storage project. The Yakama Nation filed a separate petition.

entries.title: Tribal Engagement in Transmission Planning
entries.summary: White paper on whether and how Tribes should engage in transmission planning, with a table of engagement strategies and a note that some Tribes have created Tribal utility authorities.

entries.title: Pathway to a Regional Market
entries.summary: Explains AB 825, signed September 19, 2025, which paved the way for the Regional Organization for Western Energy to govern Western wholesale electricity markets under the Pathways Initiative.

entries.title: NorthernGrid Planning Agreement for Planning Cycle 2022-2023
entries.summary: Planning agreement effective January 1, 2022. Provides for a Tribal representative eligible to vote on certain committee matters and states an intent to develop protocols for Tribal government involvement.

entries.title: Tribal Energy Summit: Advancing National Energy Goals and Tribal Sovereignty
entries.publisher: National Congress of American Indians (event listing for the Department of the Interior and Bureau of Indian Affairs summit)
entries.summary: Event listing for the Interior and BIA Tribal Energy Summit in Houston, April 29 to May 1, 2026, covering federal energy priorities on Tribal lands.

entries.title: IE Staff Out and About: Reservation Economic Summit
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Office of Indian Energy recap of the March 2026 Reservation Economic Summit. Covers a $50 million Tribal-only funding opportunity and a data center panel with Tribal enterprise leaders.

entries.title: Washington tribes seek to halt offshore wind farms
entries.summary: Reports the Northwest Indian Fisheries Commission's July 17, 2024 letter asking BOEM to halt new offshore wind discussions off Washington until Tribal concerns are addressed.

entries.title: 2025 Annual Technology Baseline: Electricity (technologies and data)
entries.publisher: NREL / National Laboratory of the Rockies
entries.summary: Consistent capital cost, O&M and capacity factor parameters (base year 2023) for wind, solar, geothermal, hydropower, nuclear and storage, with projections.

entries.title: Capital Cost and Performance Characteristics for Utility-Scale Electric Power Generating Technologies (AEO2025)
entries.summary: Overnight capital cost and fixed O&M for 19 generator types including onshore wind, solar, battery, geothermal, hydro and SMR, in 2023 dollars.

entries.title: U.S. Utility-Scale Solar, 2025 Data Update
entries.summary: Empirical utility PV and PV-plus-battery trends: 2024 levelized cost, battery capex of $458/kWh, hybrid plant adders and PPA prices.

entries.title: Tribal Electricity Access and Reliability (DOE Tribal Energy Access)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Summarizes the report to Congress: Tribal energy burden about 28% above average, about 17,000 homes without electricity, and higher outage frequency.

entries.title: Tribal Electrification Program (round two announcement)
entries.summary: Second round of the $150 million BIA Tribal Electrification Program, which funds zero-emission electricity for Tribal homes.

entries.title: Makah Tribe Strategic Energy Plan (PNNL-38051)
entries.summary: ETIPP plan with outage data, solar and wind potential, wave and biomass assessments, and resilience hub priorities for a remote Northwest coastal Tribe.

entries.title: Tribes express concern over small modular reactors in Umatilla County
entries.summary: CTUIR opposition to SMRs, waste concerns, Oregon HB 2410 context, and the unconfirmed Yakama Nation position.

entries.title: Tribes, environmentalists gather forces against Amazon's Northwest nuclear plan
entries.summary: Tribal and environmental opposition to the Amazon, X-energy and Energy Northwest SMR plan near Hanford meant to serve data centers.

entries.title: Court sides with Yakama Nation in energy appeal (Goldendale Energy Storage)
entries.summary: Washington Court of Appeals ordered a rewrite of the water quality permit for the Goldendale pumped-storage project on a site sacred to the Yakama Nation.

entries.title: Two Courts, One Conclusion: EPA Unlawfully Terminated Solar for All
entries.publisher: Sabin Center for Climate Change Law, Columbia Law School
entries.summary: Explains the September 2026 federal rulings vacating EPA's termination of the $7 billion Solar for All program, which included Tribal awards.

entries.title: Sections 45Y and 48E Beginning of Construction Notice (Notice 2025-42)
entries.summary: Guidance on when construction begins for wind and solar facilities under the July 2025 law that ends the credits for later starts.

entries.title: Generating Resource Reference Plants: Conventional Geothermal (2021 Power Plan)
entries.summary: Regional geothermal potential from the 2008 USGS assessment (identified and undiscovered MW) and risk discounts for Northwest development.

entries.title: Hydropower from a ditch? DOE sees energy potential
entries.summary: Summarizes the Oak Ridge conduit hydropower assessment: up to 1.4 GW nationally, about 530 MW online, with Washington and Oregon in the top states.

entries.title: Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure (Executive Order 14318)
entries.summary: Directs expedited federal permitting and financial support for qualifying data center projects, including FAST-41 coverage; relevant to timing of Tribal consultation.

entries.title: Joint Statement on Protecting Section 106 Process of NHPA
entries.summary: Joint statement opposing the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation's July 24, 2026 vote to advance revisions to 36 CFR Part 800, citing trust and treaty obligations and lack of Tribal consultation on the draft.

entries.title: Secretary's Order 3452: Timely Completion of National Historic Preservation Act Section 106 Reviews
entries.summary: Interior order to streamline Section 106 reviews, with deadlines and a 180-day target after which officials may consider terminating consultation. Full text was not readable in this pass.

entries.title: Indian Water Rights 101: A Summary of the Fundamentals
entries.summary: Plain-language summary of reserved rights, general stream adjudications and off-reservation instream flows needed for treaty fisheries.

entries.title: Cotton Petroleum Corp. v. New Mexico, 490 U.S. 163 (1989)
entries.summary: Held a State severance tax on a non-member oil and gas lessee was not preempted although the Tribe also taxed it; the leading dual taxation authority.

entries.title: Plains Commerce Bank v. Long Family Land & Cattle Co., 554 U.S. 316 (2008)
entries.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
entries.summary: Syllabus restating the two Montana exceptions for Tribal civil authority over non-members and limiting authority over non-Indian fee land.

entries.title: C&L Enterprises, Inc. v. Citizen Band Potawatomi Tribe of Oklahoma, 532 U.S. 411 (2001)
entries.summary: Held an arbitration clause with court enforcement language was a clear waiver of Tribal immunity; key authority for drafting limited waivers in commercial contracts.

entries.title: Washington State Department of Licensing v. Cougar Den, Inc., 586 U.S. 347 (2019)
entries.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
entries.summary: Plurality held the Yakama Treaty of 1855 right to travel preempts a Washington fuel tax; illustrates reading Stevens Treaty rights as the Tribes understood them.

entries.title: Tribal Business Structure Handbook
entries.publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Tax Exempt and Government Entities
entries.summary: Describes Section 17 corporations and limited waivers of sovereign immunity, noting courts split on sue-and-be-sued clauses. Dated 2008; verify current law.

entries.title: Announcement of U.S. Support for the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples
entries.summary: The 2010 U.S. statement understanding free, prior and informed consent as meaningful consultation, not necessarily agreement.

entries.title: Dams, data centers, climate change: Northwest Tribes confront major threats to salmon
entries.summary: Article in which Yakama Nation and CRITFC voices say data centers strain river flows, lands and energy grids and threaten treaty fishing rights. Gives no megawatt or water figures. The page shows dates of October 22 and October 26, 2026.

entries.title: Hoopa Valley Tribe Celebrates the Opening of its New Data Center, the Hub of Broadband Expansion in the Valley and Beyond
entries.summary: The Tribe's utility (HVPUD) opened a Tribally owned NTIA data center on July 17, 2026 as the operations hub for the Tribe's fiber broadband network in northern California. It is a network facility, not an AI or hyperscale campus.

entries.title: Tribe passes resolution opposing offshore wind energy development, citing impacts to fisheries, cultural resources, and heritage
entries.summary: Reports the unanimous November 2023 resolution of the Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Tribal Council opposing offshore wind as proposed and asserting a viewshed at least 12 nautical miles beyond the continental shelf. The chair says the Tribe has not taken a position on offshore wind and is at the table to learn about impacts.

entries.title: Yurok Tribal Council Votes to Formally Oppose Floating Offshore Wind Energy Projects Along the North Coast
entries.summary: Yurok Tribal Council formally opposes floating offshore wind off its coast, citing sacred cultural sites, insufficient research and risks to the Klamath headwaters. The article also cites the NCAI's February 2024 call to suspend offshore wind scoping and permitting.

entries.title: Lummi Nation Opposes BP's $50M Purchase of Culturally Significant Land
entries.publisher: Underscore Native News (originally Cascadia Daily News)
entries.summary: Lummi Nation Chairman opposes BP's purchase of about 1,100 acres at Cherry Point (Xwe'chi'eXen), citing cultural sites and treaty fishing rights. BP reported no current development plans for the land. Background on the 2016 denial of a coal terminal.

entries.title: Swinomish Announces Details of Settlement Agreement on Seattle City Light Dam Relicensing
entries.summary: Settlement on relicensing Seattle City Light's three Skagit River dams, with partner Tribes, state and federal agencies. It protects treaty fisheries and supports continued clean generation, and it goes to the Seattle City Council and then FERC. The Chairman is quoted on river health.

entries.title: Request for Proposal, Nimiipuu Energy: Nez Perce Tribal Utility Authority feasibility assessment
entries.summary: Tribal request for a consultant to assess the legal, regulatory and operational feasibility of a Nez Perce Tribal Utility Authority, including renewable energy and tariff policy. Proposals were due October 5, 2026. Read from search snippets because the PDF did not extract.

entries.title: The Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation Move Toward Energy Sovereignty with New Microgrids
entries.summary: Colville Tribes microgrid program built with an OATI platform. The chairman calls it a first step toward energy sovereignty. A separate trade article says the model could later include casinos, telecom assets and data centers.

entries.title: Data Centers: Exploring the Opportunity for Tribes
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy Policy and Programs
entries.summary: Federal guidance for Tribes presenting data center leases, power sales and jobs as opportunities. It lists water use, local impacts, transmission, interconnection and fiber access as factors to weigh. A related DOE page references a July 2026 Tribal data center exploration cohort.

entries.title: Spokane-area data center proposals, explained
entries.summary: Reports that a developer's website listed the Spokane Tribe as its first partner, then removed the Tribal partners after a screenshot circulated. The Tribe's administrative division did not respond. The developer's claims of six Tribal data centers totaling 17.5 GW by 2033 are unverified.

entries.title: Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs and Warm Springs Power & Water Enterprises Host Annual Tribal Energy Fair
entries.summary: The June 23, 2026 Warm Springs energy fair covered transmission and utility-scale initiatives meant to generate revenue for the Tribes, plus community solar, storage and efficiency projects. No data center statement is reported.

entries.title: NWPPA comments on emerging large electric loads, Docket UE-260162
entries.summary: Community-owned utility association comments to the Washington UTC favoring utility-specific large-load frameworks, citing Grant and Chelan PUD tariffs and contracts and the 2026 E3 regional study.

entries.title: Puget Sound Energy comments on large loads, Docket UE-260162
entries.summary: Investor-owned utility comments urging large-load tariffs that protect existing customers, end-use-neutral definitions, embedded-cost allocation with direct assignment, exit charges and clean-energy program funding.

entries.title: Data Center Coalition comments on large-load interconnection, Docket UE-260162
entries.summary: Industry comments arguing against regulation built on broad assumptions about one industry and asking that term, minimum billing, exit and collateral terms be assessed as one integrated package.

entries.title: IBEW Data Centers Principles
entries.summary: Union principles calling for high-road union jobs with prevailing wages and project labor agreements, fair-share energy pricing through separate rate classes, and owner-funded grid upgrades.

entries.title: Big contribution from electrical workers puts Kotek in a difficult spot
entries.summary: Reports IBEW Local 48's $400,000 contribution to Governor Kotek's campaign in June 2026 and the national IBEW's stance opposing bans on data center construction.

entries.title: Avista pauses processing of energy service request from 500 MW data center developer
entries.summary: Utility announcement pausing negotiations on a memorandum of understanding for up to 500 MW of data center load while it seeks coordinated planning with government partners.

entries.title: Oregon PUC approves PGE's large-load tariff framework for data centers
entries.summary: Reports Oregon PUC Order 26-154 approving Schedule 96 for loads above 20 MW, with 10 to 30 year contracts, 90 percent minimum capacity charges, full distribution upgrade funding and a 1 cent per kWh surcharge above 100 MW.

entries.title: Pacific Power to charge new Oregon data centers for all costs associated with growing energy need
entries.summary: Reports PacifiCorp's agreement with the Citizens' Utility Board and environmental groups to assign data center costs directly to operators, pending an Oregon PUC decision expected November 13, 2026.

entries.title: Resource Adequacy and the Energy Transition in the Pacific Northwest
entries.summary: Study prepared for a utility and independent power producer consortium; Phase 1 (September 2025) projected a resource gap of about 9 GW effective capacity by 2030 and 14-18 GW by 2035.

entries.title: Big Tech Is Trampling Native Treaty Rights to Build Data Centers
entries.summary: Reports Amazon's monthly meetings with CTUIR since 2019 and a 2023 memorandum of understanding, and argues prior informed consent falls short. Advocacy-leaning outlet; verify facts.

entries.title: Ratepayer Protection Pledge
entries.summary: Nonbinding pledge by major AI and cloud companies to build, bring or buy their power and pay full energy and infrastructure costs; later expanded to governors, legislators, developers and power providers.

entries.title: Who wants to weigh in on rates for the data centers Montana's largest utility is courting?
entries.summary: Lists parties seeking to intervene in NorthWestern Energy's large-load tariff case; names no labor, Tribal or data center developer intervenors as of late June 2026.

entries.title: It's not built yet: Yakama Nation fights $3.3B energy project and data center development on sacred site
entries.summary: Reports Yakama Nation opposition to a proposed energy and data center project on a sacred site, and developers' responses on Tribal consultation.

entries.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update
entries.summary: Modeled estimate of US data-center electricity use: 192 TWh in 2024 (4.7% of US electricity) and a 2030 reference case of 649 TWh, with a range of 521 to 843 TWh. It reports the AI-server share, an assumed training-versus-inference split, and the limits of the underlying data.

entries.title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
entries.summary: Baseline LBNL report estimating US data-center electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, with direct water use of about 66 billion liters and indirect water use near 800 billion liters. It documents the bottom-up method, server power assumptions, and a separate cryptocurrency estimate.

entries.title: Measuring the Environmental Impact of Delivering AI at Google Scale
entries.summary: Instrumented measurements of Gemini serving in production: 0.24 Wh, 0.03 gCO2e, and 0.26 mL of water for the median text prompt, counting accelerators, host machines, idle capacity, and data-center overhead. It reports a 33-fold drop in energy per prompt over one year.

entries.title: Energy Use of AI Inference, Efficiency Pathways, and Test-Time Scaling
entries.summary: Bottom-up model of frontier-scale inference on H100 servers: a median of 0.31 Wh per query (interquartile range 0.16 to 0.60), 3.91 Wh for queries 15 times longer, and 8 to 20 times potential efficiency gains. The authors find widely cited public estimates overstated by 4 to 20 times.

entries.title: The Carbon Footprint of Streaming Video: Fact-Checking the Headlines
entries.summary: IEA analysis estimating an hour of Netflix streaming in 2019 at 0.077 kWh and 36 gCO2, split 72% devices, 23% networks, and 5% data centers. It corrects earlier claims that overstated streaming's footprint by up to 90 times.

entries.title: Carbon Impact of Video Streaming
entries.summary: White paper estimating about 55 gCO2e and 188 Wh per hour of video streaming in Europe in 2020. It finds data centers, encoding, and delivery servers account for about 1 Wh, roughly 1% of the total, with viewing devices and home routers the largest shares.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence: Generative AI's Environmental and Human Effects (GAO-25-107172)
entries.summary: GAO technology assessment finding that generative AI uses significant energy and water, that companies are generally not reporting details, and that the share of data-center electricity tied to it is unclear. It sets out policy options on data collection, reporting, and efficiency.

entries.title: Google 2026 Environmental Report
entries.summary: Company report with data-center electricity of 42.4 TWh in 2025, water consumption of 10.9 billion gallons, and site-level water data including The Dalles, Oregon. It reports supply-chain emissions up 25%, mainly from hardware manufacturing and data-center construction.

entries.title: 2026 Environmental Data Fact Sheet
entries.summary: Company data tables for fiscal 2025: 37.0 TWh of electricity, 8,170 ML of water consumed, and site-level electricity and water for data centers including Quincy and East Wenatchee, Washington.

entries.title: 2025 Environmental Data Index
entries.summary: Meta's facility-level data for 2024: 18.4 TWh of electricity, 3,123 ML of water consumed on site, and 72,207 ML of water embedded in purchased electricity, the only such figure among the company reports reviewed.

entries.title: E-Waste Challenges of Generative Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Material-flow model estimating 1.2 to 5.0 million tonnes of cumulative generative-AI e-waste from 2020 to 2030, and 16 to 86% reductions from circular-economy strategies.

entries.title: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2026: Executive summary
entries.summary: Annual operator survey reporting that the most common rack density averaged just over 11 kW in 2026 (7.8 kW without high-density sites), up from 9 kW in 2025, with more operators reporting peaks of 30 kW or above. Figures are self-reported by respondents.

entries.title: The Architectural Implications of Facebook's DNN-based Personalized Recommendation
entries.summary: Characterization of recommendation models in a Facebook production data center, finding they used up to 79% of AI inference cycles in 2019. It shows that ranking and recommendation, the core of social and streaming feeds, is an AI workload.

entries.title: The Global E-waste Monitor 2024
entries.publisher: International Telecommunication Union and UN Institute for Training and Research
entries.summary: UN report estimating 62 million tonnes of e-waste generated worldwide in 2022, with 22.3% documented as properly collected and recycled, and 82 million tonnes projected by 2030. It finds e-waste recycling meets about 1% of rare earth demand.

entries.title: Oregon Data Center Task Force: Water (CTUIR)
entries.publisher: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation
entries.summary: Presentation to Oregon's Data Center Task Force that frames water as the first of the First Foods and calls for reciprocity as a requirement of sustainability. It states that surface flows and groundwater are needed to meet community First Foods goals and Tribal treaty rights.

entries.title: AI and the Power Grid: Where the Rubber Meets the Road
entries.summary: A BloombergNEF analysis of how AI-driven demand is straining power grids, with a December 2025 forecast of US data-center power demand reaching 106 gigawatts by 2035 (since superseded by a newer outlook).

entries.title: Six Things to Know About BNEF's New US Data Center Capacity Outlook
entries.summary: A BloombergNEF note on its July 2026 US data center capacity outlook, which raises forecast installed capacity to 118 gigawatts in 2030 and 194 gigawatts in 2035.

entries.title: EIA API v2, Annual Energy Outlook 2026 data route
entries.summary: The Energy Information Administration's open data interface for Annual Energy Outlook 2026, queried here for electricity purchased by commercial data center servers in the Counterfactual Baseline case.

entries.title: EIA API v2, Annual Energy Outlook 2026 data route
entries.summary: The Energy Information Administration's open data interface for Annual Energy Outlook 2026, queried here for data center server electricity use in the High Electricity Demand case.

entries.title: EIA API v2, Annual Energy Outlook 2026 data route
entries.summary: The Energy Information Administration's open data interface for Annual Energy Outlook 2026, queried here for data center server electricity use in the High Economic Growth case.

entries.title: EIA API v2, Annual Energy Outlook 2026 data route
entries.summary: The Energy Information Administration's open data interface for Annual Energy Outlook 2026, queried here for data center server electricity use in the Low Economic Growth case.

entries.title: Summer Preparedness and Long-Term Resource Adequacy Meeting Summary 2026 (Docket UE-210096)
entries.publisher: Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission and Department of Commerce
entries.summary: A Washington utilities regulator and Commerce Department meeting summary on summer preparedness and long-term resource adequacy, including a consultant study that finds a possible Pacific Northwest adequacy gap of up to 9 gigawatts by 2030 without new resources.

entries.title: Health-Informed Computing: Estimating and Addressing the Public Health Impact of Data Centers (arXiv 2412.06288 v4, formerly 'The Unpaid Toll')
entries.summary: A preprint from Caltech and UC Riverside authors that estimates the public health cost of air pollution from US data centers and AI computing, projecting a burden above 20 billion US dollars per year.

entries.title: The data heat island effect: quantifying the impact of AI data centers in a warming world (arXiv 2603.20897 v3)
entries.publisher: Marinoni et al. (preprint, not peer reviewed)
entries.summary: A preprint, not yet peer reviewed, that uses satellite data to estimate how much the land surface warms around AI data centers after they begin operating, finding an average increase of about 2 degrees Celsius.

entries.title: Assessing the Carbon Emissions and Energy Consumption of U.S. Hyperscale Data Centers
entries.summary: A preprint, not yet peer reviewed, that estimates carbon emissions and energy use at 403 US hyperscale data centers and compares their grid carbon intensity with the national average.

entries.title: Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale
entries.summary: A Google technical paper that measures the energy, emissions, and water of a median Gemini text prompt using a comprehensive method, reporting 0.24 watt-hours per prompt against a narrower method that gives 0.10.

entries.title: Microsoft 2026 Environmental Sustainability Report (FY2025)
entries.summary: Microsoft's annual sustainability report for fiscal year 2025, which reports company-wide water, energy, and emissions figures including a global average water use effectiveness of 0.27 liters per kilowatt-hour for its owned datacenters.

entries.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (LBNL-1005775)
entries.summary: The 2016 Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report that estimated US data center electricity use at 70 billion kilowatt-hours in 2014 and projected 73 billion for 2020, now superseded by later editions.

entries.title: Making AI Less 'Thirsty'
entries.publisher: Communications of the ACM 68(7) (Li, Yang, Islam, Ren)
entries.summary: A peer-reviewed article that estimates the water consumed to train and run large language models such as GPT-3, including how many responses use 500 milliliters of water.

entries.publisher: Shelby County Health Department, via EPA docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-1212
